chapter_note: The chapter is overwhelmingly a systematic cosmological-mechanical exposition of three ‘conduits/roots’ linking heavens, earths, trees, flesh, and the wheel of stars. Later material is mainly the dialogue/hagiographic apparatus (speaker attributions, disciples’ petitions). No NT citation overlay appears; the few frame formulas are detachable without disturbing the internal cosmos→cosmos mapping logic.

paragraphs.core_text: There are three conduits that exist through the entire zone, from the abyss to its heights.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again the enlightener speaks:”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula introduces a compact, impersonal numbered cosmological claim (three conduits spanning abyss→heights).

paragraphs.core_text: The first conduit is the root of all the powers above, they that exist in all the heavens. They are cast off and fettered on the earths below; because the earth below is the ‘stripping off’, the garment and the body of the powers that are above the heavens.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mechanism: conduit/root linking heavenly powers to their stripped bodies on the earths (cosmos→cosmos).

paragraphs.core_text: For when the Father of Life constructed the heavenly worlds, he divested them of their bodies, [he] threw them to the earths below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmological construction act (Father of Life) explaining the earlier mechanism; no institutional or exhortatory pivot.

paragraphs.core_text: So, the upper worlds are of the soul and the spirit; but the worlds below are of the body and the carcass [...] Now as for this, he [...] the powers of heaven; he sealed it on their bodies and their carcasses that are on the earths, so that when life comes up from the fullness of these earths, it can be entirely drawn up to the heights in the roots of what is heavenly, that are fastened in their bodies. And also, all life can be purified in that place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree/correspondence pairing (psychic/pneumatic vs somatic/ptomatic) plus a purification-transport mechanism through roots—internal system description.

paragraphs.core_text: However, the waste that will be swept from the purified one who ascends to the heights will be let fall to the ground through the conduits of these conduits, and will be poured down [...] and thrown to the underside.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic circulation schema (ascent of life, descent of residue) stated as process, not moral exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the first conduit, which comes from the powers of the heavens to their bodies and their carcasses that are upon the earth; also, from their bodies and [their] carcasses that are on the earths to the powers of the heavens.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulative definition of conduit as a bidirectional link between cosmic strata (heavens↔earths).

paragraphs.core_text: The second conduit is the one that comes from the temples and dwellings and cities that exist in the heavens down to the ground, to the five shapes of tree that grow upon the earth. The life comes up from the trees to the temples and cities. Life too, and the residue of the heavenly ones, comes down to the trees in a conduit.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic second member of a triad: heavenly ‘cities’ to five trees; still entirely cosmographic (heavenly temples/cities, not contemporary institutions).

paragraphs.core_text: And the third conduit is all the powers and householders who dwell in all the firmaments, whose roots come down from them to the five worlds of flesh that creep upon the earth, being fixed to one another. Now, the power and the life that shall be gathered in from the worlds of flesh are dispersed among them in various shapes. The powers above shall draw them to the upper side through conduits.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third member of triad; fivefold structure (five worlds of flesh) and impersonal transport mechanics mark old systematic layer.

paragraphs.core_text: [The was]te too, and the lust and the evil-doing and the anger that will be greater in the powers of [heave]n, shall be poured to the ground through their various conduits. They shall be discharged upon mankind and the other remaining animals. When what is heavenly will wash the waste and the stench and the poison down on the creations of the flesh below, in their turn the creations shall be greater in lust and anger and evil-doing against each other through the action of their fathers who are on high.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic causality of passions as descending ‘waste’ from heavenly powers; despite ethical vocabulary, it functions as cosmological mechanism (no direct exhortation).

paragraphs.core_text: Still, look at the wheel of the stars! It has no [root in this earth], but its roots are bound in the totality. The wheel of stars, then, receives life through the power and the life that ascend from the earths through conduits and the firmaments above. It (also) takes life from those conduits that receive up to the firmaments and the heavenly worlds above it, it takes life out from that place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: ‘Apostle’ attribution is compiling-frame vocabulary; the content is a structural claim about the wheel’s roots/life-supply within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: Look, in that the wheel has no root in this earth, from where did the stars and signs of the zodiac find this authority? They became masters over these five fleshes and five trees. Even though you have told us that the wheel has no root there! For you said to us that every thing, if it can be reduced from the earth, the heavenly powers above draw it through a conduit. Also, we see that every thing that a person will attain, whether it be wealth that comes into his possession or poverty that will accrue to him, or his sickness and health; he attains it through the signs of the zodiac and the star under which he shall be born.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame: “Then the disciples questioned the enlightener. They say to him:”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Disciples’ question is substantive and cosmological (zodiacal authority/fate mechanics tied to roots), though wrapped in dialogue frame.

paragraphs.core_text: Nevertheless, what I proclaimed to you, namely that the wheel has no root therein, I have recounted to you properly. It is set aright in its position. For when the Living Spirit, the Father of Life, constructed the heavens and the firmaments above, he bound their roots into the earths below; in their carcasses that he had stripped from them. Yet, when he constructed the wheel, [he] did not bind its root into the earths, but he bound the root of the wheel by the sea giant.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution: “Then he says to his disciples:”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Attribution is late frame; the explanation itself is core cosmological construction logic (Living Spirit; roots bound to carcasses; exception of wheel bound to sea giant).

paragraphs.core_text: And when [the] Ambassador came, he displayed his image and purified and brought the light out from all [the] heavens. Matter, however, which is present in all the rulers, spurted out against the image of the Ambassador. It went up in order to reach it, but reached it not. It dropped back and fell to the [under]side. Now, when it had fallen from above, it separated out into three parts.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmological episode (Ambassador’s image; Matter in rulers; threefold division) functioning as etiological mechanism inside the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The first part fell to the wheel; another part fell to the earth; an[other part fell to the se]a. [By means] of the part that fell to the sphere, [the r]oot was bound in the trees and flesh. Therefore, because of this, they received authority and became masters in the five worlds of the flesh and the five worlds of the tree.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Threefold distribution (wheel/earth/sea) and binding of roots to trees/flesh: classic structural cosmology (cosmos→cosmos).

paragraphs.core_text: Through the nature that came down [upo]n the wheel the root was bound in the trees. Also, by means of the abortions that came to the ground, another root was bound in the fleshes.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Etiology for two bindings (trees vs flesh) stated as internal causal mechanics (nature; abortions) without pastoral address.

paragraphs.core_text: Therefore, because of this, the stars and signs of the zodiac received authority over the trees and the fleshes: through the root of Sin that fell down; and [the ro]ot of the abortions that were aborted there, they fell to the ground.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Astrological authority grounded in a cosmological ‘root’ event; ‘Sin’ functions as a substantive falling entity/root rather than a mere moral label.

paragraphs.core_text: However, the[se] other conduits that [the] Living Spirit has bound in the e[a]rths, they that the soul of the elements comes up through to the heavens; those (conduits) are not bound to the wheel. Rather, they are plundered from them by the powers on the wheel, that hang from it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clarifies what is and is not bound to the wheel; again a mechanical relation among cosmic structures (Living Spirit; soul of elements; wheel-powers).

paragraphs.core_text: The first is the one that comes from the firmaments to the earths, and the one that comes from the wheel to the sea giant. That is only one. So, the other root is the one that comes [fr]om [the temples] to the trees. The third is bound by means of the abortions in the f[leshes]; also in the fleshes the fathers of the abortions who are in the heavens [...] are bound and twined, and the [y] that [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed petitionary frame: “The disciples of the enlightener say: We beseech you, our master, that just as you have instructed us and put together this lesson on [...] you have told us about the prototype of the conduits.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: A late Q&A wrapper encloses a compact structural recap of the three conduits/roots; the recap itself preserves the internal system mapping.
Pure petition formula (“We entreat you, our master…”) without independent cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: You have inquired about a [...] and you have asked about this lesson in superiority, great [...] the earth from which much life ascends [...] the Father of Life has drawn them. He has fastened them from the powers [...] he has bound them in the earths. (These conduits) are the roots of the ent[ire] ruling-power that the life of the living soul is drawn up through, it coming up from the whole earth, from all the mountains, fields and islands.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution: “The enlightener [says] to his disciples:”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Speaker tag is frame; the response is structural ranking logic grounded in cosmic ‘roots’ spanning the whole earth system.

paragraphs.core_text: After that first great root is the root of the trees, which is bound to the temples and the buildings above. For there also is much great life coming up from the tree and the entire Cross, being drawn up from them to the upper side like a great host.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Rank-order within the triad (earth-root then tree-root) plus ‘Cross’ as cosmic structure; impersonal cosmological comparison.

paragraphs.core_text: What, however, is lesser [...] of their conduit [...] he takes up [...] the roots [...] the earths, they [...] the whole earth in all the worlds. Again, these of the trees are present in the whole earth, whether small or great; but the root of mankind [...] is not present in the whole earth, other than only this world of the south. Therefore, even now these fleshes do not make [...] in the entire world of the south [...] there is a small part of them in [...] of the upper side of the world of the south in [...] in number than the [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Comparative extent of bindings (earths vs trees vs mankind) framed as cosmic geography (‘world of the south’), not institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: I have instructed you about the roots [...] them, [I] have taught you that they are bound by their [roots ...] with one another. They stir one another, they draw life from one another through the action of the powers above, which stirs the nature that dwells in them all.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding systemic statement: mutual stirring/life-transfer among bound roots via powers above—process voice characteristic of the substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, when the Matter that is in them will be crushed and despoiled, then that Matter too shall [...] its members and overturn them and [...] each other [...] stir [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary but still internal cosmological process involving personified Matter acting on ‘members’; no frame/pastoral cues.
